name: End-grain balsa (core only)
note: Wood Handbook chapter 5: balsa at 12 % moisture, bending modulus of elasticity 3,400 MPa (Table 5-5a), raised 10 % to E_L as footnote a of Table 5-1 says; elastic ratios E_T/E_L 0.015, E_R/E_L 0.046, G_LR/E_L 0.054, G_LT/E_L 0.037, G_RT/E_L 0.005 (Table 5-1); Poisson's ratio mu_LT 0.488 (Table 5-2). Density derived from specific gravity 0.16 (ovendry weight over green volume) times 1.12 for 12 % moisture, shrinkage left out. Wood varies widely between pieces; balsa sold for models is graded by weight. End grain puts the grain through the thickness; it is a sandwich core with no stiffness of its own in the panel's plane, and its shear through the thickness is the lower of G_LT and G_LR.

source.title: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook (FPL-GTR-190), chapter 5, Mechanical Properties of Wood (copy by CED Engineering)
